Reportedly, Apple hit a major milestone in India last fiscal year, with annual sales surpassing $10 billion for the first time.

This achievement is particularly striking in a country where the average annual income is less than $3,000 — especially considering iPhones are priced higher in India than in the US…

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But in recent years, that has changed dramatically as the local economy has grown and the company has finally been able to open Apple Stores in the country.

Bloomberg reported the latest milestone today.

Given India's low per capita income and the fact that iPhones are actually manufactured locally, you might expect pricing to be far lower than in the US. In reality, however, hefty taxes mean Apple products are actually more expensive in India than in the US.

Apple has been trying to offset this somewhat by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently, roughly one in four iPhones are made in India, though most are shipped to the US. Apple has restructured its logistics to sidestep US tariffs on goods imported from China.
